transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-04 16:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Jordan Park (Redwood CSM); Danielle Park (Head of Platform, Cypheron), Marcus Li (SRE), Anika Singh (Security Lead), Ravi Patel (Product).

[00:00] Liam Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll keep this to about 45 minutes, go over your availability constraints and then outline a feasible pilot, um Priya will do the technical readout.
[00:08] Danielle Park: thanks Liam, excited to chat. quick context — our product surfaces real-time scoring for recommendations, p95 needs to be under 120ms and p99 under about 300ms. We're evaluating hosted, dedicated, and private.
[00:19] Marcus Li: yeah and we have a strict on-call and incident playbook, so any degrade has to hit a fallback that doesn't leak sensitive context.
[00:26] Priya Rao: got it. quick clarifying Q — are you primarily concerned about regional outages or instance-level failures?
[00:30] Marcus Li: both, but regional is bigger for us. we want automatic region steering and a controlled fallback to a cheaper model if the hotpath is impacted.
[00:40] Liam Chen: okay so two concerns: route around region failures and graceful degradation to model-variants or cached responses. we typically recommend a multi-tier fallback: 1) local KV cache / prefix cache hit, 2) fall back to smaller quantized variant in same region, 3) route to secondary region with slightly higher latency.
[00:55] Anika Singh: can you spell KV cash? (laughs) sorry, kv cache, we want to ensure no PII stored in cache unless it's encrypted and expires quickly.
[01:03] Priya Rao: absolutely — we support prefix and KV caching with encryption at rest. we integrate with customer KMS so keys remain under your control in private and dedicated; hosted can use BYOK if needed.
[01:12] Danielle Park: BYOK, ok that's good. what about audit logs? we need request-level traceability for 90 days.
[01:18] Jordan Park: we provide per-request tracing and token-level cost/latency breakdowns — audit logs are available for enterprise tiers and can be streamed to your SIEM.
[01:26] Ravi Patel: perfect. Marcus — timeline wise we need to decide by EOY to avoid procurement season impact, so a pilot in next two weeks would be ideal.
[01:35] Marcus Li: that's the goal. can you run a 24-hour benchmark that exercises tail latencies and simulates cross-region failover?
[01:41] Priya Rao: yes, we can. we'll need your representative traffic trace and a sample prompt set. also any model variants you want to exercise — for example, primary model then a quantized fallback.
[01:52] Danielle Park: we have a 70/30 split of short/long prompts, I'll attach that. also curious about model variant fallbacks — are outputs deterministic enough? we don't want quality cliffs.
[02:03] Priya Rao: good point. our rollout patterns let you set quality thresholds — if fallback output fails evals tied to your prompt suite we'll prefer routing or retransmit logic instead of immediately degrading. quality monitoring is a first-class signal in Redwood Optimize.
[02:18] Anika Singh: security question — hosted mode, what's the default for key management and SSO?
[02:23] Liam Chen: hosted defaults to Redwood-managed keys, but we offer BYOK and HSM integrations for enterprise. SSO via SAML with SCIM provisioning is available on dedicated/private.
[02:33] Anika Singh: ok, and SOC2? ISO?
[02:36] Jordan Park: we are SOC2 Type II certified — docs in the pack I'll send. ISO in progress, and we have penetration test reports available under NDA.
[02:44] Marcus Li: great. on routing, do you support active-active between regions or is it active-passive?
[02:50] Priya Rao: both patterns are supported. active-active requires latency shaping and consistent KV cache strategy; we have a routing controller that can do region steering by policy, including capacity-based failover and cost-aware fallback.
[03:03] Liam Chen: adding that for active-active you need consistent state or a cache-warming strategy — otherwise you'll see a p50 shift when cold. we usually recommend a hot-primary / warm-secondary with fast warmup via prefix caching.
[03:18] Ravi Patel: what's the expected cost delta if we move from hosted to dedicated for our 2M tokens/day workload? rough numbers are fine.
[03:26] Liam Chen: rough ballpark, dedicated can be 30-50% cheaper per-token at scale depending on quantization and batching; but you trade off operational uplift and commitment. we'll share a pricing sheet with modeled unit economics.
[03:40] Marcus Li: okay. and SLAs — what is p99 SLA for hosted vs dedicated?
[03:45] Jordan Park: hosted provides availability SLOs and best-effort p99 targets documented per model; dedicated has contractual SLAs that include latency and uptime windows if you commit. exact numbers depend on capacity reservation.
[03:56] Danielle Park: are there built-in graceful degradation hooks we can tie into our client SDKs? we want to avoid client-side retries amplifying the problem.
[04:04] Priya Rao: yes, we expose header flags for inferred fallback states and a retry-after policy in the response; recommended client backoff and hedging patterns are included in our SDK.
[04:14] Marcus Li: one more — in the event of region partition we want an automated canary rollback to the last known-good model and circuit-breaker to stop traffic to unhealthy nodes. can Redwood do that?
[04:22] Priya Rao: yeah, rollout configuration supports automatic rollback if model health metrics cross thresholds. we also have route-level circuit-breakers and can trigger traffic-splitting to a fallback region.
[04:32] Anika Singh: on the audit side, how granular are logs? request and token-level?
[04:36] Jordan Park: request-level, with token-level cost buckets; we can include hashed prompt excerpts for debugging but we avoid storing full PII unless you opt-in and configure encryption and retention.
[04:47] Danielle Park: sounds good. what's the process to validate private/on-prem fit? we have an air-gapped environment for regulated customers.
[04:54] Liam Chen: for private we ship a customer-managed control plane package and can certify the infra blueprint. it requires a longer procurement window, typically 6–10 weeks for initial delivery and validation.
[05:05] Marcus Li: ok that's expected. can the private build include our KMS and HSM?
[05:09] Priya Rao: yes, private and dedicated support customer KMS and HSM integrations.
[05:15] Danielle Park: ok recapping next steps would be useful.
[05:18] Liam Chen: summary — we'll: 1) send security pack, SOC2, pricing and benchmark template, 2) Priya runs a 24-hour dedicated pilot with your traces once you share them, 3) follow up SLO alignment meeting next week.
[05:28] Marcus Li: yep that's right.
[05:30] Anika Singh: I will send KMS controls and compliance items.
[05:33] Jordan Park: I'll include links to our SDK hedging/backoff examples and the audit log streaming config.
[05:38] Danielle Park: thanks team.
[05:40] Liam Chen: thank you all — we'll email notes and attach the Security pack (link below).

References shared in meeting:
- Security pack & SOC2: https://redwood.ai/security-pack (will send full pack)
- Pricing sheet + unit economics template: https://redwood.ai/pricing-sheets
- Benchmark template (sample trace upload): https://redwood.ai/benchmark-template

End of transcript.
